title: Scene graph
description: Meaning representation of a short sentence, held independently of any symbol set.

id.description: Stable id, normally a hash of the normalised text.

tokens.description: Tokenisation that alignment indices refer to.

pattern.description: Dominant sentence pattern. Diagnostic only: tense, polarity and mood are orthogonal to it.

entities.description: May legitimately be empty: weather and other expletive-subject sentences assert an event with no participants.

events.description: May be empty only when speech_act is present: a bare greeting describes no scene. The validator enforces that pairing.

address.description: Who the utterance is spoken to, when the text names them. Vocatives are not participants in the event — mamma in Did you call us, mamma? is neither caller nor called — so they sit at utterance level. Held out h010, h012, h015, h045.

speech_act.description: An interactional move rather than a description of a scene. Yes and thank you assert nothing about the world, which is why 0.2.0 had nowhere to put them. A graph may carry one of these with no events at all.

alignment.description: Node to token-span map. Drives highlight-on-read, tap-a-word and the fading scaffold.

review.description: Low-confidence nodes to surface in the teacher review queue.

notes.description: Rationale for the gold annotation. Not consumed by renderers.

conceptId.description: Lemma, optionally sense-discriminated: dog, bat.animal, look-after. Resolved to art by the lexicon, never here.

quantity.description: Explicit count when stated. The renderer draws this many.

definite.description: the vs a. Kept because article use is a known ESL failure point.

deixis.description: Speaker-relative distance. With number this covers all four demonstratives: proximal+sg is this, distal+pl is those. On an entity whose concept is location it covers here and there.

gender.description: Carried only because English pronouns encode it and the figure has to be drawn. Default unspecified; never inferred from a name.

located.description: Where this entity sits relative to another, independent of any event. Covers the voice outside (h035), a basket of fine apples as apples in a basket (h026), and the music of thy voice as music from a voice (h046). Containment and source are treated spatially because that is how a picture draws them.

coref.description: Antecedent this entity refers back to.

implicit.description: Not present in the text, such as the addressee of an imperative.

comitative.description: Who the action is done along with. Held out h022, h029.

attribute.description: Asserted property, for attribution. Distinct from an entity modifier: the assertion is what a distractor has to contradict.

complement.description: Embedded event, such as the reading in: I like reading.

spatial.description: An array because one event can carry more than one figure-ground relation. Her nest is up on the bank, under the rock needs both, and 0.2.0 dropped the second, losing half the picture.

manner.description: How the action was done: slowly, still, quietly. Held out h005, h033.

frequency.description: How often. never also implies negative polarity, and both are recorded, because one says the event does not happen and the other says it never does. Held out h029, h044.

phase.description: Where the event sits in its own history: repeated, continuing, completed early, not yet. Distinct from aspect, which is about internal shape. Held out h049; again was also a Dolch gap word.

category.description: The class the theme is predicated to belong to, for X is a Y. An entity rather than a concept id so it can carry modifiers: a great storyteller keeps great, which attribute could not. Held out h041.

modifies.description: This event restricts or describes that entity rather than standing on its own — a relative clause. a house that is called a hive. Modification is not a discourse relation between two assertions, which is why discourse.type has no value for it. Held out h031, h034.

mood.description: exclamative added for How fine he looks! (h011), which 0.2.0 flattened to a statement.

degree.description: Degree on the asserted attribute. Requires attribute.

comparand.description: What the theme is compared against. Requires degree comparative.

irrealis.description: The event is not asserted to happen at all: the antecedent of a condition, or an ability rather than an action. Future tense is NOT irrealis, being asserted to happen later. The renderer must not draw an irrealis event as taking place.

spatial.description: Figure-ground relation. Prepositions are modelled explicitly because they are a primary ESL failure point and are directly renderable.

ground.description: Array form is for between, which needs two reference objects. Omitted entirely for a bare direction: fall down and Away they marched name a path with no landmark. The validator restricts which relations may leave it out.

anchoring.description: Like spatial, but the figure is the entity carrying it, so there is no figure field and a ground is always required.

role.description: Which slot the question leaves empty. The renderer draws a gap there.

inferred.description: The relation is supplied by the reader rather than marked by any word. A rule parser cannot find these, and a language model will assert them confidently, so they are held apart rather than mixed into the same pool.

degree.description: Absent means plain. very and too are kept apart because too is excessive and renders with a problem marker, while very is merely intense. Intensity and comparison are collapsed into one enum deliberately: much bigger than is beyond this reading level, and separating them now would add a field nothing uses.

modifier.description: A bare concept id, or an object when the modifier carries a degree. Consumers should normalise through the helper in tools rather than branching at each use.
